description: PRD-105: Budget & Governance — Full research + design PRD. Study cost enforcement patterns, tool policy layering, approval gates. Design per-mission budget tracking, governance rules, and human approval flows.

userStories.title: Research budget enforcement patterns
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how production systems enforce spending limits so that our budget model is realistic
acceptanceCriteria: Study AWS Budgets API — how budgets are set, tracked, alert thresholds, hard stops
Study Kubernetes resource quotas — CPU/memory limits, LimitRanges, ResourceQuotas per namespace
Study OpenAI usage tiers — rate limits, spending limits, tier progression
Study cloud billing patterns — pre-paid credits, pay-as-you-go, hard caps vs soft warnings
Document patterns applicable to LLM API cost management
Write to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: Budget Enforcement'
Include comparison of hard-stop vs soft-warning approaches with tradeoffs
userStories.notes: Our budget is primarily about LLM API costs via OpenRouter. OpenRouter returns cost info in response headers/metadata — verify this by reading the OpenRouter integration code.

userStories.title: Research tool policy and governance patterns
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how systems layer permissions and policies so that our governance model is well-designed
acceptanceCriteria: Study OpenClaw's 6-tier tool policy layering — how policies compose across levels
Study AWS IAM — policy evaluation logic, deny overrides allow, resource-based vs identity-based
Study Kubernetes RBAC — roles, role bindings, cluster roles
Study rate limiting strategies — token bucket, sliding window, leaky bucket
Document how policies could apply to: tool access, model access, budget limits, autonomy level
Write to PRD section: '## 3. Prior Art: Governance & Policy Layering'
Include policy composition model: platform → workspace → mission → task
userStories.notes: The tool_router already determines which tools an agent can access. This PRD adds governance OVER that — e.g., 'this mission can use web search but not file write'. It's a policy layer on top of existing tool assignment.

userStories.title: Design mission budget model
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the budget model designed for per-mission cost tracking and enforcement
acceptanceCriteria: Define budget fields on orchestration_runs: budget_limit (decimal), budget_spent (decimal), budget_currency (USD), budget_alert_threshold (percentage)
Define per-task cost tracking: how each LLM call's cost is captured and aggregated
Define pre-execution cost estimation: coordinator estimates mission cost before user approves
Define budget enforcement points: before task start (check remaining), after LLM call (update spent), after task complete (aggregate)
Define what happens when budget exceeded: pause mission, notify user, allow override or cancel
Write to PRD section: '## 4. Mission Budget Model'
Include cost tracking flow diagram
Include estimation accuracy expectations — 'estimates are ±50% due to variable token usage'
userStories.notes: Connect to PRD-101 orchestration_runs.config JSONB for budget settings. Connect to PRD-106 for cost telemetry. The existing TokenBudgetManager in context/budget.py manages context window tokens — this is different (API cost), but follow similar patterns.

userStories.title: Design governance configuration
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need governance rules designed so that workspace admins can control what missions can do
acceptanceCriteria: Define governance config schema: allowed_tools, blocked_tools, allowed_models, max_budget, max_tasks, max_agents, autonomy_level
Define governance levels: workspace-level (default for all missions), mission-level (override per mission)
Define approval gates: plan_approval (required/optional/skip), output_review (required/optional/skip), budget_override (who can approve)
Define how governance interacts with existing tool_router — policy filter applied AFTER tool resolution
Write to PRD section: '## 5. Governance Configuration'
Include JSON schema for governance config
Include examples: restrictive workspace (approve everything), autonomous workspace (review at end only)
userStories.notes: Keep governance simple for Phase 2 — workspace-level defaults + per-mission overrides. Don't build a full policy engine. The PRD-100 autonomy toggle (approve vs autonomous) is the key governance control.

userStories.title: Design rate limiting for missions
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need rate limiting designed so that runaway missions don't consume excessive resources
acceptanceCriteria: Define rate limits: max concurrent tasks per mission, max LLM calls per minute per mission, max total tasks per mission
Define backpressure mechanism — what happens when rate limit hit (queue, delay, not reject)
Connect to existing heartbeat rate limiting in heartbeat_service.py — similar pattern
Define workspace-level aggregate limits — total concurrent missions per workspace
Write to PRD section: '## 6. Rate Limiting'
Include sensible defaults with rationale
userStories.notes: heartbeat_service.py already has rate limiting for agent ticks. Study that pattern. Missions need similar but at a higher level — mission-level, not agent-level.

userStories.title: Write PRD-105 complete document
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to write the complete PRD-105 document
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/105-BUDGET-GOVERNANCE.md
Header, Problem Statement, synthesis of US-001 through US-005
Design Decisions Made table
Risk Register (budget estimation inaccuracy, governance friction, rate limit tuning)
Implementation Acceptance Criteria
Appendix: Budget tracking SQL examples
Appendix: Governance config JSON schema
Final review pass
PRD-105 complete and ready for peer review
userStories.notes: Follow PRD-100 style. Emphasize simplicity — Phase 2 governance should be the minimum viable policy layer.
